name: Dooru
body:
The dooru are a race of small, winged fey creatures that originate in the fey realms but they seek living near the humanoid peoples of the material planes. They are small, furry, with long ears, bat-like wings and a red orb that extends from their head on an antenna. They have their own language they use among themselves, but they adore conversing with other peoples and learn whatever language is most prevalent in the area in which they reside. They are gregarious but have a vocal tic of repeating “Dooru” at the end of any sentence they speak outside their own language. Otherwise, they are diverse and crafty people with an inordinate fear of bodies of water.

Dooru Ancestral Traits (13 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers +2 Intelligence, +2 Charisma, -2 Constitution: Dooru are gregarious and crafty but are frail.
Type: Fy (dooru). Dooru are fey with the dooru subtype.
Size: Small. Dooru are Small creatures and gain a +1 size to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty on their CMB and to CMD, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.
Speed: Slow. Dooru have a base speed of 20 feet. Additionally, dooru have a fly speed of 30 feet (clumsy).
Doo-Sight: Dooru can see twice as far as an ancestry with normal vision in conditions of dim light.
Innocent Form: A dooru receives a +1 dodge bonus against attackers who it has not threatened or attacked.
Crafty: Dooru gain Skill Focus as a bonus feat in one of the following skills: Appraise, Craft, Handle Animal, Knowledge (any), Linguistics, Perform, Profession, Sleight of Hand, or Spellcraft.
Gregarious: When a dooru successfully uses Diplomacy to win over an individual, that creature takes a –2 penalty on attempts to resist any of the dooru’s Charisma-based skills for the next 24 hours.
Hydrophobia: With their odd forms, dooru have grown a strong paranoia of drowning, and their fear is often their downfall. A dooru can hold their breath for half as many rounds as another creature of their same Constitution score, and take a -2 penalty on all swim checks. Additionally, if within sight of a body of water (with water deep enough to be up to their waist, the dooru is shaken.
Vocal Tic: All dooru are cursed with a similar vocal tic, finishing most, if not all of their sentences with the name of their race. Being a well known fact, it can often make it difficult for a dooru to hide themselves as anything but themselves. If a dooru attempts to disguise themselves as a member of another ancestry, speaking quickly begins to weaken their disguise, giving them a -2 penalty to do so.
Working Folk: Appraise and Profession are always considered class skills for dooru.
Member of the Great Doo-net (Sp) Once per day, a Dooru may cast sending as a spell-like ability with a caster level equal to their character level. The target of the sending must be another dooru with the member of the great doo-net ability.
Magical Linguist (2 RP): Dooru gain a +1 bonus to the DC of spells they cast that have the language-dependent descriptor or that create glyphs, symbols, or other magical writings. They also gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against such spells. Dooru with a Charisma score of 11 or higher also gain the following spell-like abilities (the caster level is equal to the user’s character level): 1/day—arcane mark, comprehend languages, message, read magic.
Languages: Dooru begin play speaking Common and Dooru. Dooru with high Intelligence can choose from any language as bonus languages.
Alternative Ancestry Traits
Greed: Dooru gain a +2 bonus on Appraise checks to determine the price of non-magical goods that contain precious metals or gemstones. This replaces gregarious.
Feigned Innocence: A dooru receives a +1 attack bonus against defenders who it has not threatened or attacked. This replaces innocent form.
Urbanite: Dooru gain a +2 racial bonus on Diplomacy checks made to gather information and Sense Motive checks made to get a hunch about a social situation. This replaces skill training.
Scavenger: Dooru gain a +2 racial bonus on Appraise and Perception checks to find hidden objects (including traps and secret doors), determine whether food is spoiled, or identify a potion by taste. This replaces gregarious and skill training.
